mappings.note: Red sandstone as the Mathura school's material. Sculpture, not building, so LO-103 does not apply; this is art history under the goal.

Defines the ashvamedha as a horse sacrifice performed by kings to assert sovereignty and imperial status - a political instrument. Not LO-104, because it is an established rite used for power, not a new religious idea.
Identifies the Pandyas from their capital and pearl fisheries. Dynastic and economic recall, not administration.
Traces Gandhara's hybrid style to Greek presence after Alexander - cultural contact. Not LO-103, since the item concerns sculpture rather than the construction of a monument.
Dates a coin from Central Asian dress, a Buddha image and a Greek legend to the Kushanas - reading a numismatic source. The goal's sources clause.
Mathura's wider indigenous pantheon against Gandhara's narrower Buddhist focus. Art history; LO-103's scope is buildings, not iconography.
Sorts dynasties by origin and sequence and rejects the claim about the Shakas. Chronology and political geography.

Kushana control of the Silk Route converted into imperial prosperity is a strategy of holding and profiting from territory. Not CG-SST2, because the reasoning is about what control of a route did for the state.
Statements on Bharhut's narrative reliefs, Mathura's stone and Gandhara's Greco-Roman debt. A mixed art-history set, so the goal rather than LO-103.
Kovalan as Kannagi's husband in the Silappadikaram - literary recall, part of the source base for the Tamil kingdoms.
Defines 'yaksha' as a nature spirit widely shown in early sculpture. Religious and artistic vocabulary; LO-104 would need a movement's emergence to be analysed.
The Shungas as successors to the Mauryas in Magadha - dynastic succession. Not LO-101, because no measure of governance is asked.

Reads simultaneous patronage of Vedic, Buddhist and Jain institutions as a governing approach of tolerance and inclusivity. The question asks what it says about their governance, which is LO-101 rather than the religion outcome.
Fuller indigenous Mathura figures against Hellenistic Gandhara ones. Sculptural style under the goal, not the buildings outcome.
Matches rulers to the regions they governed, keyed on Kharavela in Kalinga. Historical geography rather than administration.
A Roman buyer of pearls, spices and textiles resolved to the three Tamil kingdoms - trade history. No LO covers commerce.
Rejects political unity as a feature of the Age of Reorganisation and keeps fragmentation, invasion and cultural growth. Period characterisation.
Locates the Heliodorus pillar near Vidisha - the find-spot of a key inscription. The sources clause of the goal.
'Sangam' as an assembly of poets and scholars under Pandya patronage. Literary and source history.
Greek satraps left behind by Alexander turning their provinces into Indo-Greek kingdoms. Political narrative of how a dynasty arose, so the goal rather than an administrative measure.
Names Kharavela as the king whose year-by-year record the Hathigumpha inscription preserves. A source-identification item.
Roman coins in South India inferred as evidence of maritime trade - reading archaeological finds. Not LO-101, since no state measure is involved.
Identifies a Gandhara Bodhisattva from drapery, realism and schist. Sculptural analysis, so the goal rather than LO-103.
Matches dynasties to their contributions and rejects Kharavela as a strict Buddhist, since he followed Jainism. A factual pairing across art, script and religion, so the goal.
Accepts Mathura's indigenous style but rejects the claim that it was isolated from other traditions. Art-history judgement under the goal.
Statements on Indo-Greek coins as historical evidence, Kushana control of the Silk Route and the sequence of foreign dynasties. Chronology and sources together, so the goal rather than LO-101.
The Silk Route as the network joining China to the Mediterranean. Trade geography, which no LO in this frame covers.
Explains what a 'headless statue' is, using the Kanishka image. A point about the condition of an artefact, i.e. about evidence.
Sangam works as the earliest Tamil literature. A source-and-language recall under the goal.
Cultural confluence producing blended artistic styles such as Gandhara. A broad cultural-development judgement, not a building-technique item.
Royal emblems of the Tamil kingdoms, keyed on the Pandya fish. Dynastic symbols read from coins and inscriptions.
Roman pottery, amphorae and coins in a South Indian port read as proof of maritime trade - archaeological inference, the goal's own clause.
Rejects the Mauryas as a dynasty of this age, since the period is defined by their decline. Chronological placement.
Attributes the Grand Anicut to the Cholas. A recall of which dynasty built it; the item does not analyse irrigation as an administrative measure, which would have made it LO-101.
Defines 'assimilation' as one group absorbing another's ways. The conceptual vocabulary this chapter uses for cultural contact.
Shungas in the north and centre against Cheras in the far south. Historical geography; LO-102 would need the rulers' policies compared, not their territories.
Patanjali and the Yoga Sutras within a Shunga-period literary revival. Intellectual history under the goal.
Many simultaneous dynasties read as a fragmented landscape of regional powers. A characterisation of the period, not of any one state's administration.
A coin showing a foreign king with Shiva and Nandi read as respect for local deities. Cultural assimilation inferred from a source; LO-104 would require a new movement to be emerging.
Matches literary works to their themes and rejects the Yoga Sutras as a manual of statecraft. A source-and-text item, so the goal rather than LO-101.
